public_rationale: Later research supports Marcus's narrower expectation that new attack paths would appear after earlier fixes. IDEsaster's follow-up documents that pattern directly. It also reports that vendors successfully patched many earlier vulnerabilities. Neither finding settles the broader prediction that many attacks will remain unstopped despite even a thousand patches. No deadline was given, and the retrieved evidence does not meet the early-resolution rule.
limitations: The evidence concerns researcher demonstrations rather than a census of malicious attacks.
A vulnerability count is not a patch count.
Treating a thousand as loose emphasis would make the narrower claim easier to support, but would discard an explicit part of the wording.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Many attacks on AI coding tools won't be stopped; not even a thousand patches would suffice given the number of variations.

statement.excerpt: The bad news is that although this one was stopped, many others won’t be. No one patch would be enough, or even a thousand; there are just too many variations on the overall theme

our_interpretation: The target is attacks exploiting AI coding tools, in the context of prompt injection and tool misuse.
The ordinary reading predicts numerous successful attack variants despite extensive patching. Many does not necessarily mean most.
A thousand may be rhetorical emphasis, but it cannot silently be replaced with evidence that a few patches failed.
A controlled exploit establishes vulnerability at the time of testing; it does not by itself establish malicious exploitation or that the attack will remain unstopped.
The passage supplies no deadline or conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Documented attack and patch histories establish numerous successful variants after extensive relevant remediation, with evidence sufficient to address the claimed inadequacy of even a thousand patches.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A broadly applicable fix or independently validated architecture blocks the relevant attack family across the stated scope, undermining the claim that numerous variants necessarily escape patching. Fixing individual vulnerabilities is insufficient.

evidence.explanation: The researcher reports more than 30 vulnerabilities and 24 assigned CVEs across multiple coding products. This supports the existence of numerous attack paths, but the selected test set does not represent every product or establish a thousand-patch threshold.

The follow-up reports new extension-based attack paths after nearly 30 vulnerabilities were patched across 12 vendors. It supports recurring vulnerabilities after remediation, while the successful earlier patching is material evidence that particular attacks can be stopped.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented attack-and-remediation history addressing the scale asserted, or an independently validated general defense covering the relevant attack family.
